title: Axion detection in the non-Markovian noise
authors: Jing Dong, Shuang-Quan Ma, Rong-Hang Chen, Bin-Kai Luo, Tao Liu, Qing Ai, Jun-Hong An
abstract: The detection of axion dark matter poses a significant challenge due to its exceptionally weak coupling to standard-model particles. Here we develop a noise-tolerant quantum-metrology scheme based on coupled $^{129}$Xe spin ensembles to search for such weakly interacting particles. Within an experimentally accessible parameter regime, our scheme achieves an ideal exclusion limit on the axion coupling constant that is several orders of magnitude more stringent than that of conventional detection methods. We further investigate the performance of our scheme under dissipative noise and find that its robustness is fundamentally governed by the energy-spectrum structure of the composite spin-environment system. Remarkably, when a bound state emerges in the spectrum, the exclusion limit asymptotically recovers its ideal value in the non-Markovian dynamics, whereas under the Markovian approximation the limit deteriorates significantly due to noise. Our results establish a universal mechanism for noise-resilient exploration of beyond-standard-model physics, which can be practically implemented by engineering bound-state formation via tuning the Larmor frequency of the spin ensembles.
summary: This paper proposes a noise-tolerant quantum metrology scheme using coupled ${}^{129}	ext{Xe}$ spins to search for axion dark matter. It rigorously compares standard Markovian noise models against non-Markovian dynamics. The key finding is that the presence of a bound state in the system's energy spectrum fundamentally restores the measurement sensitivity, allowing for exclusion limits far superior to those predicted by simpler noise approximations.
main_problem: The primary challenge is detecting axion dark matter due to its extremely weak coupling to standard model particles.
main_result: The scheme demonstrates that non-Markovian dynamics, specifically when a bound state emerges in the energy spectrum, allows the measurement sensitivity to asymptotically recover its ideal, noise-free limit.
method: The analysis uses quantum metrology, calculating the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) to determine the minimum achievable magnetic-field uncertainty ($\delta B$).

important_parameters: The Larmor frequency tuning used to engineer bound-state formation; the comparison between Markovian and non-Markovian noise regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis critically compares the results derived from the Markovian approximation against the full non-Markovian treatment, highlighting the necessity of the latter.

paper_structure: The paper first introduces the detection problem and the quantum metrology setup. It then develops the theoretical framework by analyzing the system dynamics under both Markovian and non-Markovian noise. why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the fundamental issue of noise resilience in quantum sensing, providing a concrete physical mechanism (bound state formation) to overcome environmental decoherence in searches for beyond-standard-model physics.
